Unfortunately, the world did not make the strong decisions needed to help them at that time. This led to further decades of totalitarian rule across much of Europe, which ended only with the revolutions of the 1980s.

The year 1956 could have changed a great deal. This lesson now gives us grounds to say with absolute certainty: when people show courage and love of freedom, it is worth supporting. It deserves support everywhere in the world, so that freedom grows.

I thank everyone who remembers history, honors people's courage and love of freedom, and does not shy away from decisions when decisions are needed. We honor the heroes of the Hungarian Revolution of 1956!

items.tx:
BREAKING: Iran has drawn up detailed plans to attack the 7 major undersea Internet cables in the Gulf as soon as the US and Israel attack it again, per two senior Iranian officials to Reuters. 

Iran says it would aim to prevent repairs after any attack to prolong the disruption to communications and internet connections.

"If Iran is attacked, there will be no more red lines, from undersea cables to military bases, including covert ones." The official warned US not to "play with fire," saying Iran has full access to the cables and could easily destroy them.

More than 99% of international data traffic travels through undersea cables. Iran warned this month that US-linked data centres and AI facilities across the Gulf will also be targeted.

I really want our relations – between Ukraine and America, and with all our other partners – to be strong, truly friendly, and without misunderstandings. Because without a strong America that cares about what happens in the world, the world would definitely be a worse place.

qt.t: Read the full opinion here: s3.documentcloud.org/documents/2883…

items.tx:
WOW WOW WOW

Some unbelievable heavy artillery being exchanged between the majority and the dissenters here. 

An en banc decision from a 17 judge court, with a 10-7 split, we get a majority opinion, three concurring opinions, and two dissenting opinions.

Combined they total 157 pages. 

FAR too much to dissect today.

BUT, this cases raise the sole issue that was remaining on detaining illegal aliens caught in the country will removal proceedings are conducted -- whether the Due Process Clause of the Fifth Amendment requires that they be given a bond hearing even if the statutory language used by Congress specified otherwise. 

The cases SCOTUS has agreed to take up involve only what the statute's require in terms of a bail hearing -- not whether due process requires one even if the statutes do not. 

But some Judges granting bail hearings have entered alternative rulings when ordering the release of aliens while removal proceedings are underway. Their orders state that even if they are wrong on what the statute requires, the 5th Amendment Due Process clause requires a hearing before liberty can be deprived for such aliens.

This en banc decision by the Fifth Circuit raises the issue -- which the SCOTUS could now decide to take up at the same time it is going to the statutory cases.
